about.body: The 300Tdi is Land Rover's 2.5-litre turbocharged four-cylinder diesel engine, produced from 1994 to 1998. It's the direct successor to the 200Tdi and was fitted exclusively to the Defender (L316) during its production run. The 300Tdi is a mechanically injected diesel engine using a VE fuel injection pump, not common-rail — it's from the generation of engines where timing belt interval is critical because it's an interference engine. If the timing belt breaks, pistons collide with valves. The engine is also known for head gasket issues and turbocharger bearing wear on higher-mileage examples. We rebuild these engines from strip-down through to reassembly, replacing timing belts, bearings, gaskets, and seals as standard.

byModel.body: The 300Tdi was fitted exclusively to the Defender (L316) during its 1994–1998 production run. This is a single-application engine — every 300Tdi we work on is from a Defender of this era. The engine's mechanical injection system and interference design mean timing belt maintenance is critical, which is why timing belt replacement is always part of our rebuild scope.

compatibility.body: Because the 300Tdi was only fitted to one model generation — the Defender (L316) from 1994 to 1998 — compatibility is relatively straightforward compared to engines that span multiple platforms. However, registration/VIN matching is still required to confirm you have the correct variant and to ensure all ancillaries match your specific vehicle's configuration.
compatibility.boldNote: We always confirm by registration/VIN before any rebuild or replacement.
